question: Which accessibility standard and conformance level does your product meet, and what evidence supports that claim?
Does your conformance include the criteria added in WCAG 2.2, such as focus not obscured, minimum target size, dragging alternatives, redundant entry and accessible authentication?
Does your accessibility claim cover every user role and surface, including donor and advisor portals, staff back office, administrator tools, mobile use and embedded partner widgets?
Are third-party components embedded in your product, such as payment forms, identity verification or chat widgets, included in your accessibility evaluation?
Can every journey be completed at 400 percent zoom or on a 320 CSS pixel wide screen without horizontal scrolling or loss of content, including complex tables?
Can you provide a current VPAT or Accessibility Conformance Report, and which edition (WCAG, Section 508, EN 301 549 or international) does it use?
Who prepared your ACR, was it validated by an independent accessibility specialist, what product version and date does it cover, and what testing methods does it rest on?
Will you update the ACR with each major release and notify us when conformance changes?
How do you test accessibility: which automated tools, what manual review, and what assistive technology testing?
Which screen reader, browser and platform combinations do you test with, including mobile screen readers?
Do people with disabilities participate in usability testing of your product?
Are accessibility checks part of your build pipeline, and can a release proceed with known accessibility regressions?
Where AI agents write or modify user-interface code, how do you ensure their changes do not introduce accessibility failures?
Do your designers, developers, testers and support staff receive accessibility training appropriate to their roles?
How can our staff or end users report an accessibility barrier, and how quickly will you respond?
What are your remediation timeframes for accessibility defects by severity, and will you commit to them contractually?
Do you publish a roadmap for known non-conformances, with target dates?
While an accessibility defect remains open, what equivalent alternative do you provide so affected users can still complete the task?
Are statements, contribution acknowledgments, grant letters and reports produced as tagged PDFs that conform to PDF/UA, and how is that verified?
Is every document also available in an accessible HTML form with the same content, and can a user prove it is the same document as the PDF?
Are data exports, charts and dashboards accessible, for example with structured headers in exported files and text or table alternatives for charts?
Are notification emails and correspondence templates accessible, including semantic structure, sufficient contrast and a plain-text alternative?
Who is responsible for the accessibility of documents uploaded by us, our donors or charities, and does your product help identify inaccessible uploads?
How does your design system or component library enforce accessibility, for example contrast-checked color roles, visible focus, forced-colors support and correct semantics?
If we apply our own brand colors and logos, how do you prevent our branding from making the product fail contrast requirements?
Does the product respect user settings such as reduced motion, high contrast or forced colors, and text spacing overrides?
Can you support a federal agency buyer's Section 508 obligations, including a 508-edition ACR and conformance of electronic content and software?
As a public entity subject to the DOJ rule requiring WCAG 2.1 AA for web content and mobile apps, including content we provide through contractors, can you meet that standard by our compliance date?
Have you received accessibility demand letters, complaints or lawsuits, and how do you allocate accessibility litigation risk with customers who serve the public?
Do you provide services to consumers in the EU that fall within the European Accessibility Act, and if so, how do you meet its requirements and publish the required accessibility information?
Will you warrant accessibility conformance in the contract and commit to remediation if the product falls short?
Are your support channels and help documentation accessible, for example accepting relay calls, offering text-based support and providing documentation in accessible formats?

Can users with disabilities complete sign-in, multi-factor authentication and identity verification without solving puzzles, memorizing codes or using a smartphone, while reaching the same security level?
Do session timeouts warn users and allow extension, and how do you balance that with security limits during long tasks such as grant submission?
Does the product use an accessibility overlay or automated remediation widget, and will you commit not to add one as a substitute for conforming code?
Does the system enforce double-entry accounting so that every journal entry balances before it can be posted?
Do journals balance within each individual fund and restriction class, not only in total for the organization?
How are multicurrency transactions recorded and balanced, and can currency conversion change the source transaction amount?
Is balance enforced in the database itself, so that a defect or direct database access cannot persist an unbalanced journal?
What dimensions must every journal line carry (for example entity, fund, program, restriction, currency), and how are invalid combinations rejected?
Can posted journal entries be edited or deleted by any user, administrator or vendor employee?
How are accounting errors corrected, and is the original entry preserved with a link to its correction and the reason and approval for it?
Can you produce the ledger as it was known on a past date, separately from the ledger as later corrected for that date?
How would you detect that ledger records were deleted, reordered, duplicated or altered outside the application, for example by a database administrator?
How do schema migrations and database deployments protect ledger tables and their append-only protections from being dropped or weakened?
Does the system support nonprofit fund accounting under FASB ASC 958, including net assets with and without donor restrictions?
How do you determine whether amounts received into a donor-advised fund are contribution revenue or a liability (agency or pass-through)?
Does the platform treat donor-advised fund balances as donor-restricted net assets by default, and who decides the classification?
How are pledges, conditional contributions and grant commitments distinguished from cash and settled assets in the books and in amounts available for grants?
How is the amount a donor sees as available to recommend derived, and can it differ from the fund's general ledger balance?
When does the system recognize grant expense and grants payable, and can each sponsor configure that recognition point?
How do you produce a period-end cutoff listing of grants approved, communicated, unpaid and conditional?
Can a donor's grant recommendation ever create a liability or payment without sponsor approval?
How do you prevent transactions from being posted into a closed accounting period?
Who can reopen a closed period, under what conditions, and how is the reopening evidenced?
How are transactions that arrive after a period closes but relate to it (for example a late custodian statement) recorded?
What must be reconciled and resolved before a period can be certified as closed, and can unresolved breaks be overridden?
Is there a race condition between period close and in-flight postings, and how is it prevented?
How are year-end audit adjustments proposed by our external auditor recorded, and are passed adjustments tracked?
When a posting rule or accounting policy changes, how is the effect on prior periods handled and documented?
How are material errors in previously issued statements corrected while preserving the statements as originally issued?
How do you verify that posted journals still match what the approved posting rules would have produced from the source events?
Does the ledger support multiple legal entities with intercompany or interfund transactions and eliminations for consolidated reporting?
How are different sponsors' ledgers segregated so that one customer's postings, balances or reports can never include another customer's data?
If our existing ERP remains our general ledger of record, how does your platform avoid creating a competing authoritative book?
When funds transfer between sponsors, such as a fund moving to another sponsoring organization, how is each side's ledger kept complete and independent?
What support do you provide to our external auditors, such as read-only access, standard audit schedules and transaction drill-down?
Can you trace any figure on a fund statement or financial statement back to the individual source transactions and supporting evidence?
How do you reconcile Form 990 Schedule D donor-advised fund figures to the audited financial statements and individual fund statements?
If a report is reissued months later, how do you prove it is identical to the version previously delivered to donors or auditors?
Can the platform map its accounts to our chart of accounts and export journal entries to our general ledger system?
How do you ensure that a GL export is complete and that every exported entry is received and posted in our system?
How are changes to the account mapping controlled and versioned, and can historical exports be reproduced under the mapping in effect at the time?
Does your platform replace our general ledger, or is it designed to feed it, and which accounting functions are out of scope?
Does each AI agent operating in your environment have its own unique identity, separate from human user accounts and not shared between agents?
Can you attribute every production and source control action to a specific agent, model version, prompt version and initiating person?
When an agent acts on behalf of a user, do records show both the agent and the user it represents?
How are credentials issued to AI agents, how long do they live, and how quickly can they be revoked?
When one agent delegates work to another, how do you preserve attribution and stop the delegate from gaining more authority than the delegator?
Are agent action logs tamper-evident, retained as audit evidence and available to us for actions on our data?
How are the permissions of each AI agent defined, who approves them, and where are they recorded?
Is there any path, including configuration changes, tool calls or persuading a human operator, through which an AI agent could obtain additional permissions or approve its own output?
Is authorization for agent actions enforced by deterministic code outside the model, or does it depend on the model following instructions?
What is the highest-impact action an AI agent can execute in your platform today without a human?
How often are agent permissions reviewed, and are unused permissions removed?
What happens when an agent repeatedly requests actions beyond its authority? Is that ever escalated into an approval?
Which actions in your service always require approval by an authorized human, and can any configuration, agent or emergency path bypass that?
Can an AI agent approve a grant, release a payment, change bank or payee details, or instruct a trade?
Can AI clear or close a sanctions alert, fraud flag or eligibility concern, or can it only raise one?
Does a human approval apply to the exact proposal and evidence the approver saw, so that any later change to amount, recipient or facts requires reapproval?
How do you prevent people from approving AI-prepared items without meaningful review?
Do you enforce segregation of duties between an agent that prepares a transaction, the human who approves it and the process that reconciles it?
Can we delegate routine decisions to deterministic rules instead of humans, and is that delegation recorded with board authority, limits and expiry?
Can you immediately stop one AI agent or all AI agents, and what happens to actions already queued or in progress?
If AI services or providers are unavailable, do your core processes continue to work?
Who is authorized to invoke an agent emergency stop, and who approves resumption?
How often do you test the agent emergency stop, and can you show the results?
For each consequential decision, can you show who was accountable, what evidence they saw, what AI contributed and which policy version applied?
Can a donor, advisor or grantee challenge a fact that AI contributed to a decision affecting them and obtain human review?
Do your records and screens distinguish verified facts from AI inferences, recommendations and decisions?
Can you reproduce a past decision, with its inputs and versions, for our auditor or examiner?
Is any control or audit evidence you provide generated, summarized or interpreted by AI? How do we know it is accurate?
How do you distinguish evidence produced by deterministic systems from content produced or interpreted by AI?
Can AI agents create, modify or delete audit evidence or logs?
Is test or synthetic evidence clearly separated from production evidence in what you show auditors and customers?
When an AI-produced summary or extraction is found to be wrong, how is it corrected and how are assertions that relied on it withdrawn?
Were these questionnaire responses prepared with AI? Who reviewed them and who is accountable for their accuracy?
How do you ensure your responses do not describe planned controls as if they were already operating?
Will an officer of the company attest in writing to the accuracy of these responses?
For each response, can you show the evidence and sources that support it?
Can AI coding agents merge code to protected branches or deploy to production without approval from a human?
Who is accountable for code written by AI agents, and does a human review every change to security- or control-relevant parts of the system?
Do AI agents perform production operations such as incident response, configuration changes or data corrections? With what approvals?
How do you prevent the same agent or model session from both authoring and approving a change?
Are AI agents ever given break-glass or emergency privileged access?
Do you use AI tools to process the questionnaires, security addenda, contracts or policies we send you, which providers receive them, and under what retention and training terms?
Do you maintain an inventory of every AI system, model and AI-enabled feature used to deliver or support the services you provide to us?
Does your AI inventory include AI used internally to build, test and operate the service, such as AI coding agents and AI operations assistants, and not only AI features exposed to customers?
For each AI use, which data classes can it access, which provider hosts the model, and which model version is in use?
How do you detect and prevent unapproved AI tools (shadow AI) receiving customer data from your personnel or contractors?
When a model version, provider, prompt or tool changes, how quickly is the AI inventory updated, and how is completeness verified?
Can you give us a customer-specific list of the AI components and AI providers that process our data?
Do you have a formally approved policy governing the development, procurement and use of AI? Who approved it and when was it last reviewed?
Who is the accountable executive for AI risk, and how does AI risk reach senior management or the board?
What rules govern your personnel entering our confidential data into AI tools, and how are those rules enforced technically?
What AI literacy training do your personnel and agent operators receive, and how is completion tracked?
How are exceptions to your AI policy requested, approved, time-limited and recorded?
Have you aligned your AI risk management to the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, including the Generative AI Profile? Can you share the mapping?
Are you certified to ISO/IEC 42001, and if not, do you plan to be? What scope and timeline?
Has any independent party assessed your AI governance or AI controls, for example a SOC 2 examination covering AI agents or an ISO/IEC 42001 audit?
Do you map your AI controls to the CSA AI Controls Matrix or a similar control catalog that we can compare across vendors?
Before deploying an AI capability, do you perform a documented risk assessment covering accuracy, security, privacy, bias and misuse? Who approves it?
Do you assess the impact of your AI systems on individuals affected by them, such as donors, advisors, grantees and employees?
Is AI used to make, or to be a substantial factor in, any decision about an individual's eligibility, access to services, financial outcome or employment?
How do you test automated matching or scoring, for example sanctions name matching, for higher false-alert rates on particular name origins or groups?
What events cause an AI risk assessment to be repeated, for example a model change, new data source, new use or incident?
Which third-party AI model providers do you use, and what due diligence did you perform on each before use?
Do you obtain and review SOC 2 or equivalent assurance reports from your AI providers, and how do you implement their complementary user entity controls?
Before adopting a model, do you review its documentation, such as system cards, evaluation results and known limitations, against your intended use?
How do you detect and control provider-initiated model updates or deprecations so that model behavior does not change in production without your review?
If you use open-weight or third-party models, how do you assess their license and acceptable use terms against your commercial use?
Do the AI providers you use retain prompts and outputs that contain our data, and for how long?
Is our data used by you or any AI provider to train, fine-tune or improve models? Is that prohibited by contract?

question: Do AI provider terms allow provider staff to review prompts for abuse monitoring, and have you obtained zero-retention or opt-out terms where available?
Will you use our data to train, tune or evaluate your own models, agents or prompts, including building evaluation sets?
Have you determined whether any of your AI systems are high-risk under the EU AI Act, and whether you act as provider or deployer?

Does Colorado's automated decision-making technology law (SB 26-189, which repealed and reenacted the Colorado AI Act) apply to any of your systems as a developer or deployer, and what documentation will you provide to us as deployer?
How do you track new state laws on AI and automated decision-making and assess whether they apply to you or to our use of your service?
As an insurer, we must oversee third-party AI systems under our AI program. Will you provide documentation, testing information and audit cooperation for AI used in services you provide to us?
Do any of your AI features interact directly with people or generate content in a way that triggers EU AI Act transparency duties, and how do you meet them?
Does any part of your service produce outputs that we should treat as a model under our model risk management policy, and will you support our validation of it?
Can you provide documentation for independent validation of your models: purpose, design, data, assumptions, limitations, performance testing and monitoring?
Do you perform ongoing performance monitoring and outcomes analysis of your models, and will you share the results with us?
Will you notify us in advance of material changes to models, prompts or AI providers so we can update our model inventory and revalidate?
Do you disclose where AI is used in the service you provide and in your own operations, including whether AI writes your software?
Are AI-generated outputs labeled as such in the product and in communications sent to our donors, advisors or grantees?
Can we disable AI features for our tenant without losing core functions?
Will you notify us before introducing new AI features or AI providers that process our data, and can we decline them?
Do you measure or estimate the energy use and environmental footprint of the AI features and AI tools used to deliver the service, and will you disclose it to us?
How do you protect AI features in your service against direct prompt injection and jailbreak attempts by users?
How do you prevent instructions hidden in uploaded documents, emails, charity records or retrieved web pages from being followed by your AI components?
If a prompt injection succeeds, what is the most harmful action the affected AI component could take?
Do you rely primarily on prompt instructions, filters or classifiers to stop injection, or on architectural limits on what the AI can do?
Can AI-generated narrative alter, hide or reorder deterministic findings, such as sanctions or eligibility results, that are presented to human approvers?
Do your system prompts contain secrets, credentials or authorization logic, and what happens if a user extracts them?
How do you protect your AI coding agents from instructions planted in issues, pull requests, dependency documentation or web pages they read while working?
How do you ensure an AI feature serving one customer cannot retrieve or reveal another customer's data?
Are embeddings and retrieval indexes segregated per customer, and is authorization re-checked at retrieval time rather than only at indexing?
Is prompt or response caching, including any provider-side prompt caching, scoped so cached content cannot be served across customers?
Do your AI assistants or agents keep persistent memory between sessions, and how is that memory scoped, reviewed and deleted?
Do AI coding or operations agents ever have access to production customer data, for example while debugging? Under what conditions and approvals?
How do you test for data leakage between customers through AI features, and how often?
Which tools or functions can your AI components call, and how is the tool set restricted per task?
Are AI tool calls authorized with the same server-side checks as the human user they act for, or with a privileged service identity?
How do you prevent an AI agent from altering sensitive parameters, such as an amount, payee, bank account or permission, when it calls a tool?
Can any AI component send data outside the service, for example by email, web requests, or by rendering links and images that call external URLs?
How do you limit AI resource consumption, such as tokens, tool calls, time and cost, to prevent runaway loops or denial-of-wallet attacks?
Is model output treated as untrusted before it is rendered, stored or passed to another component?
Can model output ever be executed as code, database queries, shell commands or HTML anywhere in your service?
How do you prevent AI-generated content from causing cross-site scripting or data exfiltration in the browser?
How do you prevent AI output from being stored or displayed as if it were an authoritative record or decision?
How do you detect and limit fabricated or incorrect facts in AI outputs shown to us or our donors?
How do you verify the integrity and provenance of the models, AI libraries and agent frameworks your service depends on?
Does your SBOM, or a separate AI bill of materials, list models, datasets and AI SDKs with versions?
How do you vet third-party tool servers, plugins or connectors that your AI agents use, including servers based on the Model Context Protocol?
How do you protect retrieval corpora, fine-tuning data and evaluation sets from poisoning?
How do you protect the credentials your AI agents use to reach model providers, tools and repositories, and can an agent read or leak them?
Have you threat-modeled your AI features against the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications 2026? Can you share coverage?
Which MITRE ATLAS techniques have you assessed as applicable to your service, and how is each mitigated?
How do you monitor AI features in production for abuse, jailbreak attempts, anomalous tool use or data extraction?
Do you conduct AI red teaming? Who performs it, how independent are they, how often, and can we see a summary of results?
Do you run an automated adversarial test suite for prompt injection and authority escalation that blocks release when it fails?
Are AI features and agent integrations in scope of your external penetration tests?
How are AI-specific findings, including jailbreaks reported by outside researchers, triaged, fixed and retested?
How much of your production code is written by AI coding agents, and which agents and models are used?
Is code written by AI agents subject to the same or stronger review, testing and security analysis as human-written code? Who reviews it?
How do you prevent AI coding agents from adding non-existent, typosquatted or malicious packages to your software?
How do you prevent AI coding agents from disabling tests, weakening security checks or editing CI configuration to make a build pass?

subcategory: Secret and data exposure to coding assistants
question: How do you prevent secrets, credentials or customer data in developer environments from being sent to AI coding assistant providers?
Do your language and architecture choices limit the kinds of vulnerabilities that AI-generated code can introduce? Which classes are removed and how is that enforced?
Is access to model artifacts, prompts, fine-tuning data, retrieval corpora and evaluation datasets limited to named roles and jobs, and is every read and change logged?
Which parties do you screen against OFAC sanctions lists: donors, advisors, successors, grantee organizations, grantee principals, payees and payors?
When is screening performed: at onboarding, whenever lists change, and before each disbursement?
Is screening performed at the moment of an irreversible disbursement, and can a match found during release stop the payment?
Which lists do you screen against, for example the SDN list, OFAC consolidated non-SDN lists, and UN, EU or UK lists?
How do you address the OFAC 50 percent rule for entities owned by blocked persons when screening grantees and other organizations?
Do you screen the officers, directors and bank account holders of grantee organizations, or only organization names?
How quickly after OFAC publishes a list update is it applied to your screening?
Does each screening result record which list version was used and when it was fetched?
What happens to disbursements if the list data is stale or the screening service is unavailable?
Where do you obtain list data, and how do you verify its integrity and completeness?
What name matching method do you use, including fuzzy, phonetic and transliteration handling, and how are match thresholds set?
How do you test that screening actually catches listed names and their variants, and who approves the results?
Are changes to matching logic or thresholds change-controlled, tested and approved before use?
Do you measure false-alert rates by name origin or other subgroups to detect disproportionate impact on particular donors or grantees?
How are secondary identifiers such as date of birth, address, country and EIN used in screening and alert resolution?
Is AI or machine learning used in matching or alert scoring, and can it ever close an alert on its own?
Who reviews potential sanctions matches, what qualifications and authority do they have, and within what timeframe?
What does a disposition record contain, and does it show the facts the reviewer compared rather than a score?
When a true match is confirmed, how are funds blocked or a transaction rejected, and how are the required reports to OFAC prepared within 10 business days?
Do you reuse previous false-positive decisions for repeat matches, and when do those decisions expire?
What does a donor see when a grant is held for sanctions review?
Is there a second-level review or quality sample of sanctions dispositions?
How long do you retain screening results, alert dispositions and blocked or rejected transaction records?
Can you produce the complete screening history for a given party or transaction for an examiner or auditor?
Are screening and disposition records protected from alteration after the fact?
Are you subject to Bank Secrecy Act anti-money laundering program requirements yourself?
Can your platform support our customer identification and customer due diligence requirements, including beneficial ownership for entity donors?
Do you monitor for suspicious activity, such as structured contributions or rapid pass-through to grants, and how are alerts provided to us for SAR decisions?
How do you protect the confidentiality of any suspicious activity information, and prevent tipping off, in your platform and among your personnel?
Will you support our independent AML testing and regulatory examinations with data, documentation and access?
Do you support grantee due diligence consistent with Treasury's anti-terrorist financing guidelines for U.S.-based charities?

For grants to foreign organizations or through intermediaries, what diligence is supported, such as equivalency determination or expenditure responsibility, sanctions licenses and anti-corruption checks?

Do you treat donor-directed benefits, such as grants that pay a donor's personal pledge, tuition, event tickets or a related organization's expenses, as red flags for misuse of the fund, and how are they escalated?
Do you detect patterns such as split grants, repeated grants to the same recipient, or contributions quickly followed by grants that may indicate layering?
How do you detect charity impersonation and verify changes to a grantee's bank account or contact details?
How do you prevent grants to intermediaries from being earmarked for a specific foreign organization chosen by the donor?
How does every API operation verify that the caller is entitled to the specific object identified in the request, and how is this tested for every endpoint?
Can an API credential issued to one sponsor or partner ever return or modify data belonging to another sponsor, including through search, export, bulk or reporting endpoints?
Do API responses return only the properties the caller is entitled to see, and are writes restricted to properties the caller may change?
How are administrative and privileged API functions separated from ordinary functions, and how do you test that lower-privilege callers cannot invoke them?
Do AI agents and automated integrations call the API under their own identities with their own authorization rules, or do they borrow user or service credentials?
Is API authorization deny-by-default and enforced at one central point, or implemented separately in each endpoint handler?
Are object identifiers exposed in APIs unguessable, and do you rely on that unguessability for any access decision?
What authentication methods does the API support for partner systems, and which are permitted for operations that affect money or donor data?
How are partner API keys issued, scoped, stored, rotated and revoked, and can a sponsor see which keys exist for its tenant and when each was last used?
Are access tokens sender-constrained (mutual TLS or proof of possession) or plain bearer tokens, and what are their lifetimes?
How do you detect and respond to a partner credential that appears in a public repository, log or ticket?
How does the API validate tokens (issuer, audience, signature algorithm, expiry), and is the algorithm fixed server-side?
How are API authentication endpoints protected against credential stuffing and brute force?
Do you enforce rate limits on API endpoints, at what granularity (user, client, tenant, IP), and what response does a caller receive when limited?
How do you bound expensive API operations such as large exports, searches, report generation and document rendering so one caller cannot degrade service for others?
Which business flows are protected against automated abuse independent of request rate (for example adding payees, grant recommendations, account recovery), and what limits apply?
Can sponsors or partners configure their own limits on API-originated activity (value per day, recipients per period), and are limits enforced on the server?
Do any API calls trigger paid third-party services (identity verification, data lookups, AI models), and how do you prevent abuse that drives cost?
Are API requests validated against a published schema before processing, and are responses validated so internal fields cannot leak?
Do you maintain an inventory of all API hosts, versions and environments, including deprecated and non-production endpoints reachable from the internet?
What is your API versioning and deprecation policy, how much notice do customers receive before breaking changes, and how are emergency security changes handled?
Is the published API documentation generated from or verified against the implementation, so that no undocumented operations exist?
Do you run contract tests against partner integrations so schema changes on either side are detected before production?
Do you provide a non-production API environment for partner testing, and is it guaranteed to contain no real donor or financial data?
Are webhooks you send signed, how can recipients verify them, and how are signing keys rotated?
How do you verify the authenticity of inbound webhooks and files from banks, custodians and partners, and can an inbound event by itself change an authoritative record or approve anything?
What prevents a captured webhook or partner message from being replayed later?
How do you treat data returned from third-party APIs (charity data providers, identity verification, custodians): validated as untrusted input, or trusted?
What happens when webhook delivery fails repeatedly, and can delivery retries or redirects be used to reach unintended destinations?
Do mutating API operations support idempotency keys, and what happens if the same key is reused with a different payload?
If a client times out after submitting a payment- or grant-affecting request, how does it determine safely whether the request took effect?
Are idempotency guarantees carried through to banks, payment processors and partners, or do they stop at your API boundary?
How do you ensure API hosts do not expose debug endpoints, verbose errors, default credentials, permissive CORS or outdated TLS in production?
Can any external API call approve a grant, release a payment, post to the ledger or change permissions directly, or must it pass through an approval workflow?
When AI assistants or agents use your API, what prevents them from performing operations reserved for human approval, and is this enforced by the platform rather than by prompts?
Does any integration with the service, or with our accounts at other institutions, require donors or advisors to share their login credentials with you or with a third-party tool?
How does the application prevent SQL injection across all database access paths, including reporting, administrative and batch components?

Is any SQL constructed by string concatenation or interpolation anywhere in the codebase, including database functions using dynamic EXECUTE, migrations and operational scripts, and how would you know?

Your standard says all database access goes through Strata. Which component actually executes application queries today, how is a bypass (raw Npgsql, a second connection string, a reporting tool with direct credentials) detected, and what reproducible evidence scopes the elimination claim?
How do you test for second-order injection, where data stored safely is later used unsafely in a query, report, search filter or export?
Does your secure development process require that bespoke software be protected against injection attacks, and can you show evidence of this for the release we will use?
Does any application component invoke an operating system shell or external process, and if so, how are arguments constructed and constrained?
Can any user, partner or AI agent input reach a dynamic evaluation facility such as expression evaluators, scripting engines, runtime compilation or dynamic assembly loading?
Are document, email or notification templates (including sponsor-customizable white-label templates) rendered with an engine that can evaluate expressions, and how is template injection prevented?
How do you prevent injection into logs, HTTP headers, directory queries and other interpreters (CRLF, LDAP, XPath) where user input is written?
What exceptions to the no-shell and no-dynamic-code rule exist in build tooling, deployment automation or operational scripts, who approved them, and when do they expire?
How does the application prevent stored, reflected and DOM-based cross-site scripting?
Is output encoding applied according to context (HTML body, attribute, URL, JavaScript, CSS), and which component is responsible for each context?

Your standard says the platform never accepts user-supplied HTML. How do grant purpose notes, donor messages and sponsor-authored content support formatting, and what prevents a future feature from adding an HTML or Markdown renderer?
Do you deploy a Content Security Policy, and does it permit unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval or broad source allowlists? If WebAssembly requires evaluation permissions, what exactly is allowed?
Which channels other than the web UI render user-controlled text (PDF statements, acknowledgment letters, emails, CSV exports, partner embeds), and how is each protected against injection?
When your interface is embedded in a partner or sponsor site, how is script isolation maintained and how do you prevent the host page or your component from injecting script into each other?
How are state-changing requests protected against cross-site request forgery?
What SameSite, Secure, HttpOnly and prefix attributes are set on session and authentication cookies, and how is drift detected after deployment?

What is your cross-origin resource sharing policy, does any endpoint reflect arbitrary origins or allow credentials from origins you do not control, and how is the allowlist governed for partner domains?
How do you prevent the application from being framed by unauthorized sites to trick users into approving actions?
Which features cause the server to make requests to URLs or hosts influenced by users, partners or AI agents, and how are destinations restricted?
Is outbound network access from application workloads restricted at the network layer as well as in code, and are cloud instance metadata endpoints unreachable from application processes?
How do you test SSRF defenses against redirects, DNS rebinding, IPv6 and decimal or octal IP encodings, and alternate URL schemes?
Can an AI agent or assistant feature fetch arbitrary URLs or call arbitrary tools, and how are its outbound requests constrained and logged?

For a zero-day in a widely used component, how quickly can you determine exposure across every deployed version and tenant, and what is your emergency remediation process?
When a vulnerability cannot be remediated within SLA, how are exceptions requested, approved, time-limited and tracked?
Who has authority to accept the risk of an unremediated critical vulnerability, and is that authority separated from the engineer responsible for the fix?
Are customers informed when an accepted vulnerability risk affects a control they rely on, such as a complementary user entity control?
Can an AI agent approve, extend or close a vulnerability exception or scanner suppression, and what prevents an agent from suppressing a finding to make a gate pass?
Do you publish a vulnerability disclosure policy that tells external researchers how to report issues, what is in scope, and what legal safe harbor applies?
Do you publish a security.txt file at the standard well-known location on your domains, and are its contact and expiry fields kept current?
What acknowledgment and status-update timelines do you commit to for external vulnerability reports, and how do you coordinate public disclosure with the reporter?
Are externally reported vulnerabilities routed into the same tracking, prioritization and SLA process as internally found ones?
If a vulnerability is reported in one of your published libraries (for example Aegis, Limen or Strata), how is it handled, and are downstream users notified?
Do you operate a paid bug bounty program, public or private, and if so on which platform and with what scope?
If you do not run a bug bounty, what compensates for the absence of continuous external adversarial attention?
How do you prevent bug bounty or researcher testing from touching real customer data in production?
Will you notify us when a vulnerability affecting the service or our data is discovered, and what will the notice contain?
Do you publish security advisories for vulnerabilities fixed in the service, and do you obtain CVE identifiers for vulnerabilities in software you distribute?
During a widely publicized vulnerability event, how quickly will you answer our inquiry about exposure, and through which channel?
Do you notify customers of vulnerabilities in subprocessors or hosting platform components that affect the service, even when the fix is the provider's responsibility?
How quickly do you apply security updates to the application runtime, database engine, container base images and operating systems, and how do you verify that every instance was updated?
Do you patch by rebuilding and redeploying immutable artifacts rather than changing running systems, and how do you detect drift between deployed and patched builds?
Do you track end-of-support dates for runtimes, frameworks and the database engine, and plan migrations before support ends?
When AI agents propose or implement vulnerability fixes, how do you verify that the fix is correct and complete and does not introduce new weaknesses, and who is accountable for it?
Are vulnerabilities in the AI tooling used to build and operate the service (model SDKs, agent frameworks, tool integrations) tracked in the same vulnerability program?

Will you accept our non-intrusive monitoring of your internet-facing assets, such as attack surface scanning, open-source intelligence and threat hunting, and how do you receive and act on findings we send you?
Which surfaces can be white-labeled (portal, mobile, email, statements, acknowledgments, embedded components), and what remains vendor-branded?
Can a sponsor or partner rename legally meaningful concepts, for example calling a grant recommendation a 'donation' or hiding the sponsor's legal name?
Are white-label portals served from sponsor-controlled custom domains, and who manages certificates and DNS?
How does the platform ensure branded themes remain accessible (contrast, typography) to WCAG 2.2 AA?
Does the white-labeled experience disclose that a technology provider operates the platform, and where?
In a co-branded or partner-branded experience, how are donors told which organization legally owns the assets and approves grants?
Who reviews partner-authored marketing and interface text that describes sponsor actions, and against what standard?
Can a partner display fund balances or grant status in its own interface, and how is accuracy assured?
Is the platform registered as a charitable fundraising platform in states that require it (for example California and Hawaii), and does it meet their disclosure duties?
When emails are sent under a sponsor's or partner's brand, who is the legal sender and how are commercial email obligations met?
How do embedded components prevent being framed by unauthorized sites, and is the frame-ancestors policy specific to each partner origin?
How does the platform protect confirmation steps against host-page overlays that trick donors into submitting grants?
How are messages between the host page and the embedded component validated, and what data is exposed to the host?
How is an embedded session established, how long do launch tokens live, and can they be replayed?
Does the embedded component trust the host's assertion of who the user is, or does it independently authorize every action?
If an advisor's access is revoked while an embedded widget is open, how quickly does the widget stop showing data and accepting actions?
What content security policy and third-party script restrictions apply to the embedded component itself?
How do embedded sessions work under browser third-party cookie restrictions without weakening session security?
How is our institution's client data isolated from other partners and sponsors on the platform?
What isolation options exist (separate schema, separate database, dedicated infrastructure), and can a partner move between them without changing identifiers?
How does the platform determine which tenant a request belongs to, and can a client manipulate that?
Which services are shared across tenants (identity, charity registry, search, telemetry, support tools), and what partner data do they hold?
Can one partner's data be restored or exported without affecting or exposing others?
When several partners distribute the same sponsor's DAF program, how are partners isolated from each other's donors?
What donor data does a distribution partner (bank, broker, advisor platform) receive, and in what form?
May a partner use donor data obtained through the platform for its own marketing or advice?
When a partner relationship ends, what happens to donor data the partner holds?
How is a partner's user identity linked to a donor's fund, and how are mapping changes controlled?
Can wealth-management partners see fund holdings for advice purposes, and how is that access scoped and logged?
How do partner systems authenticate to the platform's APIs, and how are credentials scoped, rotated and revoked?
Can a partner API call approve a grant, move money or change sponsor policy?
How are partner API capabilities limited to what the partner's contract entitles, and what happens when an entitlement is removed?
Are partner commands idempotent and partner events signed and replay-protected?
When a partner's employee or advisor leaves, how quickly is their access removed end to end?
How are partner API and event schema changes versioned and communicated so partner integrations do not break silently?
What rate limits and abuse protections apply to partner APIs?
What must a partner complete before its integration goes live (security, copy review, accessibility testing)?
If a partner is suspended (for example after a breach), what happens to donors' in-progress actions and how are donors informed?
When a distribution partner ends its relationship, how are donors' funds handled, and can funds move to another sponsor?
Is accessibility tested for the combined host page and embedded component, not just the component alone?
Can a partner or sponsor obtain a complete export of its data when the relationship ends?
